prompts.prompt_text: I have a Dialog component that takes 12 props including isOpen, onClose, title, description, children, size, variant, showOverlay, closeOnEscape, closeOnOverlayClick, initialFocus, and returnFocus. Should I use compound components or keep the flat props API?
Survey the current component library for pattern violations. Focus on spacing inconsistencies, color token misuse, and accessibility gaps.
Extract the design system tokens from the existing codebase. Focus on color palette, typography scale, spacing scale, and border radius conventions.
Design the motion for a notification toast that appears from the top-right, persists for 4 seconds, and can be dismissed by swiping. The action is reversible (undo available).
Design the physics for a drag-to-reorder list. Items should feel weighty but responsive. Consider the snap-back behavior when a drag is cancelled.
Implement a dark mode solution for the dashboard. The current implementation uses Tailwind dark: classes but we need to support user preference AND system preference with a toggle.
The spacing in the sidebar feels inconsistent. Some items use gap-2, others gap-3, and the section headers have mixed padding. Decompose the spacing issues and propose fixes.
Extract the design taste from the current codebase into a taste.md file. Analyze color usage, spacing patterns, typography choices, and motion conventions.
Apply the taste tokens from taste.md to the new Settings page component. Flag any conflicts between the taste direction and the component requirements.
Capture the design direction from stripe.com and linear.app as visual references. Identify common patterns, tensions between the two, and synthesize a coherent direction.
Run an accessibility audit on the DataTable component. Check for keyboard navigation, screen reader support, focus management, and ARIA attributes.
Review the Next.js application for performance anti-patterns. Check for waterfall fetches, barrel imports, unnecessary client components, and missing Suspense boundaries.
